precepts.text: Elijah was taken up by a whirlwind into heaven; that is what it means that God took Enoch.
precepts.point: Enoch walked with God and was not: the Most High took him up, and Enoch did not taste death, the same way Elijah did not taste death.

note.label: Genesis 5: The Book of the Generations of Adam

precepts.why:
Elijah did not taste death, and neither did Enoch. Elijah told Elisha, “if thou see me when I am taken from thee, it shall be so unto thee”; and as they still went on and talked, “there appeared a chariot of fire, and horses of fire, and parted them both asunder; and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.”

That is what it means that God took Enoch. “Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him.” The Most High took him up, the same way Elijah was taken up by a whirlwind into heaven.

precepts.text: Elisha asked for a double portion of Elijah's spirit before his master was taken from him.
precepts.point: It was the same in the time of Christ: the apostles taught like Christ, and men could tell that spirit was on them, just as the elders carried the spirit of Moses.
precepts.why:
The Lord “took of the spirit that was upon him, and gave it unto the seventy elders: and it came to pass, that, when the spirit rested upon them, they prophesied, and did not cease.” The same thing happened with Elijah and Elisha.

Elisha was Elijah's right hand and disciple. Before Elijah was taken up, “Elijah said unto Elisha, Ask what I shall do for thee, before I be taken away from thee. And Elisha said, I pray thee, let a double portion of thy spirit be upon me.” The spirit that was on the master passed to the disciple, as the spirit that was on Moses passed to the elders.

precepts.text: The sons of the prophets saw it and said, The spirit of Elijah doth rest on Elisha.
precepts.point: It was the same in the time of Christ: the apostles taught like Christ, and men could tell that spirit was on them, just as the elders carried the spirit of Moses.
precepts.why:
When the spirit of Moses rested on the seventy elders, they prophesied. When the spirit of Elijah rested on Elisha, it could be seen too: “And when the sons of the prophets which were to view at Jericho saw him, they said, The spirit of Elijah doth rest on Elisha. And they came to meet him, and bowed themselves to the ground before him.” They saw Elisha smite Jordan with the mantle and knew whose spirit was on him.

It was the same in the time of Christ: the apostles taught like Christ, and men could tell that spirit was on them, just as the elders carried the spirit of Moses.

“There came forth little children out of the city, and mocked him, and said unto him, Go up, thou bald head”: go up means get out of here. Little children have no filter. For the prophet to curse them in the name of the Lord, he was mad, because these little children were evil. “And there came forth two she bears out of the wood, and tare forty and two children of them”: a she bear with cubs is worse than the male, relentless. God didn’t just send any bears, he sent two she bears.

points: When the Most High is about to take up Elijah into heaven by a whirlwind, Elijah goes with Elisha from Gilgal and tells him to tarry, but Elisha refuses to leave him. At Bethel and at Jericho the sons of the prophets tell Elisha that his master will be taken from him today, and each time he answers that he knows it and bids them hold their peace.

note.label: 2 Kings 2: Elijah Taken Up and a Double Portion for Elisha

points: The sons of the prophets are a prophetic order or company, not the literal blood sons of the prophets. Fifty of them stand afar off to view as Elijah and Elisha come to the Jordan.

note.label: 2 Kings 2: Elijah Taken Up and a Double Portion for Elisha

points: Elijah takes his mantle, wraps it together, and smites the waters, which divide so the two go over on dry ground. Elijah asks what he shall do for Elisha before he is taken, and Elisha asks for a double portion of his spirit; Elijah says it is a hard thing, granted only if Elisha sees him taken. A chariot of fire and horses of fire part them, and Elijah goes up by a whirlwind into heaven.

note.label: 2 Kings 2: Elijah Taken Up and a Double Portion for Elisha

points: Elisha sees it and cries, my father, my father, the chariot of Israel and the horsemen thereof, and sees him no more. He takes hold of his own clothes and rends them in two pieces and takes up the mantle of Elijah that fell from him.

note.label: 2 Kings 2: Elijah Taken Up and a Double Portion for Elisha

points: Elisha returns and smites the waters of Jordan with the mantle, asking, where is the Lord God of Elijah, and the waters part so he goes over. The sons of the prophets at Jericho see it and say the spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha, and they bow themselves to the ground before him.

note.label: 2 Kings 2: Elijah Taken Up and a Double Portion for Elisha

points: The sons of the prophets press Elisha to let fifty strong men go and seek his master, in case the spirit of the Lord has cast him upon some mountain or valley. Elisha tells them not to send.

note.label: 2 Kings 2: Elijah Taken Up and a Double Portion for Elisha

points: They urge him until he is ashamed, and he lets them go, but after three days they do not find Elijah. When they return, he reminds them that he told them not to go.

note.label: 2 Kings 2: Elijah Taken Up and a Double Portion for Elisha

points: The men of Jericho tell Elisha that the city is pleasant but the water is bad and the ground barren. Elisha calls for a new cruse with salt in it, casts the salt into the spring, and says, thus saith the Lord, I have healed these waters; there shall not be from thence any more death or barren land.

note.label: 2 Kings 2: Elijah Taken Up and a Double Portion for Elisha

points: The waters are healed to this day according to the saying of Elisha. The sign shows that the spirit that was on Elijah now works through Elisha.

note.label: 2 Kings 2: Elijah Taken Up and a Double Portion for Elisha

points: As Elisha goes up to Bethel, little children come out of the city and mock him, saying, go up, thou bald head. He turns back, looks on them, and curses them in the name of the Lord.

note.label: 2 Kings 2: Elijah Taken Up and a Double Portion for Elisha

points: Two she bears come out of the wood and tear forty and two of the children. Elisha goes on from there to Carmel and returns to Samaria.
